packs.title: Survival Basics
packs.goal: Get through the first day politely before you can build long sentences.
packs.context: These are ready-to-say chunks. Learn them as whole phrases first, then notice the grammar later.

words.english: It's okay. / That's all right. / No, thank you.

example.ko: A: 죄송해요. / B: 괜찮아요, 그럴 수도 있죠.
example.en: A: I'm sorry. / B: It's okay, these things happen.
example.romanization: A: joesonghaeyo. / B: gwaenchanayo, geureol sudo itjyo.

example.ko: A: 이제 가 볼게요. / B: 네, 안녕히 가세요.
example.en: A: I'll head off now. / B: Take care, goodbye.
example.romanization: A: ije ga bolgeyo. / B: ne, annyeonghi gaseyo.

words.english: Goodbye (said by the person who is leaving).

example.ko: A: 먼저 가겠습니다. 안녕히 계세요. / B: 네, 안녕히 가세요.
example.en: A: I'll be heading off now. Goodbye (stay well). / B: Take care, goodbye.
example.romanization: A: meonjeo gagetseumnida. annyeonghi gyeseyo. / B: ne, annyeonghi gaseyo.

example.ko: A: 이 길로 가면 돼요? / B: 네, 맞아요.
example.en: A: Do we go this way? / B: Yes, that's right.
example.romanization: A: i gillo gamyeon dwaeyo? / B: ne, majayo.

packs.title: Survival Help
packs.goal: Stay calm when you do not understand, need help, or need one practical sentence fast.
packs.context: These phrases keep the conversation alive when Korean gets too fast.

words.english: I'm not sure / I don't really know.

example.ko: A: 이거 어디다 두면 돼요? / B: 저도 잘 모르겠어요. 사장님한테 물어봐야 할 것 같아요.
example.en: A: Where should I put this? / B: I'm not sure either. I think we need to ask the boss.
example.romanization: A: igeo eodida dumyeon dwaeyo? / B: jeodo jal moreugesseoyo. sajangnimhante mureobwaya hal geot gatayo.

example.en: I'm sorry, I'm not good at Korean.
A: How much is it? / B: It's 4,500 won.

packs.title: Numbers Starter
packs.goal: Read prices, counts, simple dates, and clock-hour basics without waiting for a full number chapter.
packs.context: Native numbers handle people, things, age, and hours. Sino numbers handle dates, prices, minutes, phone numbers, and addresses.

example.en: Which of the two do you like more?
I'll count to three. One, two, three!
There are six pieces of candy.
Count to ten and open your eyes.
Lend me just a thousand won.

packs.title: Family Words
packs.goal: Name close people naturally when introducing yourself or asking about someone.
packs.context: Family words are common in real Korean because age and relationship shape how people address each other.

example.en: My dad works at a company.
My father is an office worker.

packs.title: Body Basics
packs.goal: Say what hurts, describe people, and understand basic health phrases.
packs.context: Body words become practical when paired with 이/가 아파요, 괜찮아요?, and simple description.

example.en: My older sister's face is really pretty.
I sat for a long time so my shoulder hurts.
I carried a heavy bag so my arm hurts.
My finger got caught in the door so it hurts.
I climbed a lot of stairs so my knee hurts.

packs.title: Time And Days
packs.goal: Understand today, tomorrow, weekdays, and simple appointment timing.
packs.context: Time words are often used without particles in speech, but 에 appears when you point to a specific time.

example.en: I drink coffee in the morning.
I watch a movie in the evening.
I usually rest on the weekend.
The day after tomorrow is Thursday.

packs.title: People And Places
packs.goal: Recognize the people and places that appear in first conversations and errands.
packs.context: These nouns support N이에요/예요, 에 가요, 에 있어요, and simple identity sentences.

example.en: I am sick, so I go to the hospital.
Let's eat lunch at this restaurant.

packs.title: Home And Things
packs.goal: Talk about your room, belongings, and everyday objects around you.
packs.context: These words pair with 있어요/없어요, 주세요, 에, and simple adjective descriptions.

example.en: There's a laptop on the desk.
Please have a seat on this chair.

example.ko: 저는 침대에서 안 자고 바닥에서 자요.
example.en: I don't sleep in a bed, I sleep on the floor.
example.romanization: jeoneun chimdaeeseo an jago badageseo jayo.

example.en: Please take your shoes off when you come in.
I put the book into the bag.
I write my name with a pen.
One moment, let me turn on the computer.
It's raining. Do you have an umbrella?

packs.title: Food Basics
packs.goal: Read menus and say simple food preferences or restrictions.
packs.context: Food words become useful immediately with 주세요, 먹어요, 마셔요, 맛있어요, and 못 먹어요.

example.en: I eat rice in the morning.
I want to eat meat tonight.
I eat a lot of vegetables.
I eat bread in the morning.
How much is a tray of eggs?
I drink tea in the morning.
How about a glass of beer?
I want to eat Korean food.
What would you like to drink? Shall I get you a drink?

packs.title: Color Words
packs.goal: Describe objects by color in shopping, clothing, and everyday descriptions.
packs.context: Color nouns sit directly before the noun: 검은색 가방, 빨간색 우산. 까만색 is a vivid everyday synonym for black.

example.en: It snowed in winter so the world is white.

example.ko: 오늘 하늘이 회색이라 비 올 것 같아요.
example.en: The sky is gray today, so it looks like it'll rain.
example.romanization: oneul haneuri hoesaegira bi ol geot gatayo.

example.en: The cherry blossoms are pink, so they're really pretty.
The orange umbrella stands out well.

packs.title: Agreeing & Understanding
packs.goal: Show you're listening — half of a real conversation is reacting, not producing new sentences.
packs.context: These look interchangeable but are not: 맞아요 confirms a fact, 그러게요/그러니까요 agree with an opinion, 그렇군요 takes in something new.

example.ko: A: 이 길로 가면 돼요? / B: 네, 맞아요.
example.en: A: Do we go this way? / B: Yes, that's right.
example.romanization: A: i gillo gamyeon dwaeyo? / B: ne, majayo.

words.english: Right? / exactly / I know, right — agreeing that you feel the same, often a bit helplessly.

example.ko: A: 오늘 진짜 덥다 / B: 그러게.
example.en: A: It's really hot today / B: Right?
example.romanization: A: oneul jinjja deopda / B: geureoge.

words.english: Exactly / that's what I'm saying — emphatic agreement with someone's opinion or complaint.

example.ko: A: 요즘 배달비가 너무 비싸요 / B: 그러니까요. 음식값보다 더 나올 때도 있어요.
example.en: A: Delivery fees are so expensive these days / B: Exactly. Sometimes it comes out higher than the food.
example.romanization: A: yojeum baedalbiga neomu bissayo / B: geureonikkayo. eumsikgapsboda deo naol ttaedo isseoyo.

words.english: I see / so that's how it is — calmly taking in information you've just been told.

example.ko: A: 이 건물은 주말엔 문을 닫아요 / B: 아, 그렇군요. 몰랐어요.
example.en: A: This building closes on weekends / B: Ah, I see. I didn't know.
example.romanization: A: i geonmureun jumaren muneul dadayo / B: a, geureokunyo. mollasseoyo.

words.english: Me too / same here — saying that what they just said about themselves is true of you as well.

example.en: A: Nice to meet you / B: You too.

words.english: I think so / It seems that way.

example.ko: 오늘 비 올까요? — 그런 것 같아요. 아침부터 하늘이 어두웠거든요.
example.en: Will it rain today? — Seems like it. The sky has been dark since morning.
example.romanization: oneul bi olkkayo? — geureon geot gatayo. achimbuteo haneuri eoduwotgeodeunyo.

words.english: Oh good / What a relief / I'm glad to hear that (relieved that things turned out okay)

example.ko: A: 시험 통과했어요. B: 아, 다행이네요.
example.en: A: I passed the exam. B: Oh, what a relief.
example.romanization: A: siheom tonggwahaesseoyo. B: a, dahaengineyo.

words.english: Oh good, that worked out — reacting on the spot to a situation turning out well.

example.ko: A: 다음 주에 재택근무 해도 된대요 / B: 잘됐네요! 출퇴근 시간 아끼겠어요.
example.en: A: They said I can work from home next week / B: Oh, that's great! You'll save the commute.
example.romanization: A: daeum jue jaetaekgeunmu haedo doendaeyo / B: jaldwaenneyo! chultoegeun sigan akkigesseoyo.

example.ko: 요즘 진짜 피곤하죠? — 그렇죠, 요즘 일이 너무 많아요.
example.en: It's really exhausting lately, right? — Exactly, there's just too much work.
example.romanization: yojeum jinjja pigonhajyo? — geureochyo, yojeum iri neomu manayo.

packs.title: Reacting & Surprise
packs.goal: React like a person, not a textbook — the difference between a chat that dies and one that keeps going.
packs.context: 진짜요? and 정말요? both mean 'really?' — 진짜요? is warmer, 정말요? is the safe neutral pick.

words.english: Really?! / for real? — surprised, more colloquial and emotional than 정말요.

example.ko: A: 나 로또 됐어 / B: 진짜?!
example.en: A: I won the lottery / B: For real?!
example.romanization: A: na rotto dwaesseo / B: jinjja?!

words.english: Really? — a polite check that you heard right, mild surprise or interest.
Oh really? / is that so? — light surprise plus a nudge for the other person to tell you more.

example.ko: A: 저 그 영화 벌써 봤어요 / B: 아 그래요? 어땠어요?
example.en: A: I already saw that movie / B: Oh really? How was it?
example.romanization: A: jeo geu yeonghwa beolsseo bwasseoyo / B: a geuraeyo? eottaesseoyo?

words.english: Whoa / OMG / no way — a gut reaction of shock, disbelief, or mild dismay.

example.ko: A: 나 폰 잃어버렸어 / B: 헐.
example.en: A: I lost my phone / B: Whoa.
example.romanization: A: na pon ireobeoryeosseo / B: heol.

words.english: Awesome! / wow / no way — a big reaction to something amazing, shocking, or extreme.

example.en: A: I got promoted / B: Awesome!
No way, is it already sold out?

words.english: Oh my / oh! — a quick gasp of surprise, more neutral and usable than 헐.
Oh right! — the sound of a forgotten thing suddenly surfacing in your own memory.

example.ko: A: 내일 몇 시에 만나요? / B: 아 맞다, 저 내일 병원 가야 돼요.
example.en: A: What time should we meet tomorrow? / B: Oh right — I have to go to the hospital tomorrow.
example.romanization: A: naeil myeot sie mannayo? / B: a matda, jeo naeil byeongwon gaya dwaeyo.

words.english: No way / that's ridiculous / unbelievable — strong disbelief at something absurd or shocking.

example.ko: A: 그 사람이 1등이래 / B: 말도 안 돼.
example.en: A: They say that person came first / B: No way.
example.romanization: A: geu sarami 1deungirae / B: maldo an dwae.

words.english: Oh no, what do we do

example.ko: A: 지갑을 잃어버렸어요. / B: 어머, 어떡해요!
example.en: A: I lost my wallet. / B: Oh my, that's awful!
example.romanization: A: jigabeul ireobeoryeosseoyo. / B: eomeo, eotteokaeyo!
